why: Which Temporal namespace a workspace's runs live in (ADR 0051 §2: the namespace is the isolation boundary, and the only one Temporal enforces for us). TWO WRITERS that must agree byte for byte: `control/orchestrator/src/workspaces.ts::namespaceFor`, which every API read and every orchestrator worker resolves through, and the CLI's `namespaceForWorkspace` in `cli/internal/config`, which `kontra workflow serve` and `kontra workflow start` resolve through. If they disagree, a workflow is served in one namespace and started in another: the start succeeds, nothing polls it, and the Run sits at RUNNING with an empty page.
rule: The workspace named `default`, and an install with no named workspace (``), keep the legacy namespace: `KONTRA_NAMESPACE`, or `default` when it is unset or blank. That is ADR 0051 §6 — every Run that existed before isolation stays readable there. Every other workspace is `ws-<name>`, whatever `KONTRA_NAMESPACE` says, because a custom legacy namespace names that ONE install's old address, not a prefix for new ones. A name the workspace rule refuses is refused here too, rather than turned into a namespace.

cases.why: no named-workspace layout, nothing configured: today's behaviour, unchanged
no named-workspace layout, a configured namespace: still honoured
blank counts as unset, as `??` alone would not
the workspace called default keeps the legacy namespace and every Run already in it
the seeded starter on a fresh install is NOT legacy: it gets its own address
a configured legacy namespace is not a prefix for other workspaces
hyphens survive: a namespace may hold them

refused.why: an underscore, which the workspace rule forbids so two names cannot share one catalog
